items.title: Lawrence Cotton Interview, 1996-12-10
items.q: He was out there playing ball with Alfred Collins

ctx.x: Well I had a brother who was at 616 Bell Castle Street. He was out there playing ball with Alfred Collins and some other guys. He ran after the ball. The man's backing out didn't see him and the truck ran over him. He got crushed. And it wasn't too long after that that we moved back to 822 Bell Castle. And like I said my dad he left and we stayed there until 1968 and we moved over. That single house that we acquired back then in 1978 and we got this 822 where we first, when my mother saw the address up there.

How did you describe it? How did you describe it? Oh the house I grew up in was a shotgun, a double, shotgun double. Oh so you were on one side? Yeah we were on one side and another family on the other side. Yeah. The Day's family. My aunt used to live there first.
